title: Establishment and evaluation of structured, long-term follow-up for children and adolescents with congenital heart disease
summary:
Compared to their healthy peers, patients with complex congenital heart defects are more likely to suffer from neurocognitive and psychosocial deficits in the long term. These late effects can sometimes occur years later and should be recognized and treated as early as possible. We are therefore planning a healthcare research project to improve the holistic long-term care of children and their families with complex congenital heart defects.
We are planning an open, prospective, monocentric cross-sectional study using questionnaires and non-invasive and radiation-free physical examinations of children who have undergone heart and/or aortic surgery at our clinic in previous years due to complex cardiac anomalies.
The research project is not subject to any special legal regulations. Study duration: 2-3 years. 
The aim is to conduct a needs assessment in two subprojects with regard to neurocognitive and psychosocial challenges for patients and their families over the long-term. To date, there is no generally applicable needs-based aftercare structure for patients with AHF in Germany that takes both neurocognitive and psychosocial outcomes into account. 
In subproject A, 40-50 patients who underwent a mechanical circular stroke in the years 2000-2024 are to provide standardized information on their subjective well-being, health support needs and family stress experience using questionnaires.
In subproject B, 25 patients 10 years after complex aortic arch surgery will also be evaluated using the above-mentioned questionnaires and, in addition, the indication for extended diagnostics in a socio-pediatric center will be examined. 
Outlook: Structured, multidisciplinary long-term follow-up care could enable risk reduction for late effects to be detected and treated earlier in follow-up studies. In addition, with better knowledge about their illness and their risk of late effects, these patients could develop greater health-related self-efficacy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Subproject A: 
Patients: Living patients
Treatment period: 2000-2024
Treatment location: Clinic for Congenital Heart Defects and Pediatric Cardiology, University Heart Center Freiburg/Bad Krozingen (University Medical Center Freiburg)
Cause of treatment: Heart failure
Type of treatment: Mechanical circulatory support (Extracorporeal Life Support System = ECLS) 
Declaration of consent by the patient and/or parents/legal representatives.

Subproject B: 
Living patients
Treatment period: 2014-2017
Special feature: Have already been included and examined in the study/preliminary investigation “Influence of rewarming rate during cardiac surgery in deep hypothermia of infants with AHF” (application no. EK-Freiburg 452/14).
Declaration of consent by the patient and/or the parents/legal representatives.
Exclusion criteria:
Subproject A: 
Patients: Deceased patients
Diseases: Pre-existing neurological abnormalities, seizure disorders, patients with chromosomal aberrations.
Lack of informed consent

Subproject B: 
Deceased patients
Missing declaration of consent
Patients with chromosomal aberrations
